messages.content:
You are walking along a straight corridor 1.75 m wide. Another person, Person 2, is walking towards you, facing you, 6 m ahead, in the middle of the corridor, as you are. Person 2 says: "I'll keep to my right." Which way do you move, left or right?

Answer on the first line with your answer only (a word, a short phrase or a lane number), then give one sentence saying why on the next line.

raw_output:
Right
Because Person 2’s right is your left, so you move to your right to pass clear of them.

They say keep to my right means to Person 2's right side. From my perspective, since facing opposite, their right is my left. If Person 2 moves to their right, they occupy (from my view) my left side of corridor. To avoid, I should move to my right? Need avoid collision. Then I should move to my right (+x) to increase separation. So answer: right. But need consider simultaneous? If he keeps to his right (my left), I should keep to my right. They ask "Which way do you move, left or right?" likely right. Need final first line answer only and sentence why. 
Need be cautious about conventions: "my right" from Person 2? Person says "I'll keep to my right" facing you. If he moves right relative to his body, then from your perspective left. So you move right. Yes. If he says I'll keep to my right, does that mean as seen from you? No.
